- **AWS account onboarding: welcome mail, direct and guided risk assessments** — the "new AWS account discovered → mail the owner and start an assessment" path becomes a three-mode capability, and the scoping decision moves to the person who actually knows. `WELCOME_ONLY` sends a welcome mail from a classpath template; `DIRECT` additionally starts an assessment for a use case the operator names (today's behaviour); `GUIDED` mails the owner a **one-time, expiring link** whose answers resolve through admin-configured rules into a *set* of use cases, and creates the assessment only on submit, scoped to the **union** of every matching rule. All three run from CLI (`--onboarding-mode`, `--welcome-email`, `--questionnaire-expiry-days` on `import` and `import-s3`), REST and MCP, all dry-runnable, plus a first-class `simulate-onboarding` verb (CLI + REST + MCP `simulate_account_onboarding`) that runs the whole path against a made-up account id and address — the *same* code path a real import runs, not a mock, which is what makes it a rehearsal and why it is rate limited, audited, and stamps every simulated mail with "this is a test, sent by <actor>". **The backward-compatibility contract is the load-bearing part**: a caller sending only `startRiskAssessment=true` — every `extensions/` client, `import-s3`, both existing E2E drivers — resolves to `DIRECT` **with no welcome mail**, byte-identical to before, reconciled in one function (`AccountOnboardingMode.resolve`); an explicit non-`DIRECT` mode combined with that flag is rejected, never guessed. **The matcher never decides**: it sees only choice ids (a BOOLEAN question is two choices, no second code path), every matching active rule contributes and nothing wins, `priorityOrder` is display order only, the single `isDefault` rule is consulted **after** everything else fails, and a resolution producing no requirements in the ACTIVE release is an error rather than an empty questionnaire. Answers that match nothing are **persisted** and the invite stays usable, so an admin can add the missing rule and the owner's original link still works. Rules are normalized tables, not a `ruleJson` blob (`DemandClassificationRule`'s precedent exists for a recursive condition; this one is a flat AND over choice ids, and the rule→use-case link needs real FK integrity). **The public questionnaire is the first genuinely unauthenticated write path in the codebase** and is treated as such: 256-bit `SecureRandom` token (not `UUID.randomUUID()`, because this token *creates* an assessment), single use enforced by a guarded UPDATE **claimed before** creation, 14-day expiry, a byte-identical 404 for malformed/unknown/expired/used/cancelled so the endpoint is no enumeration oracle, the account id **masked** to four digits and the owner email never returned, a new bounded fixed-window rate limiter with a dedicated failed-lookup bucket, `@Secured(IS_ANONYMOUS)` explicit on every method plus an `intercept-url-map` entry so a stale `secman_auth` cookie cannot 401 an owner out of their own link, and the full token never logged, never returned by any API, never printed by the CLI, never in an MCP result and never minted by a dry run — all asserted. Unanswered invites get one reminder then lapse; **nothing is ever auto-created**, because an assessment scoped by a guess looks authoritative and is not. `createAssessment` now takes `useCases: Set<UseCase>` (`use_case_name` widened 255→1024 in V253) and `sendStartNotification` was promoted to `notifyAssessmentStarted` so the guided path reuses the identical mail. Five private helpers were extracted from `AwsAccountRiskAssessmentService` into `EmailTemplateRenderer` — with a **closed template allowlist**, because the basenames are operator config and interpolating one into `getResourceAsStream` would be a classpath-traversal read — and the twice-copied recipient regex into `EmailAddressValidator`. New: ADMIN-**or-SECCHAMPION** admin API and UI (a deliberate widening vs Demand Classification's read-both/write-ADMIN, with a coverage matrix that shows which answer combinations would dead-end *before* an owner hits one), `/onboarding/[token]` public page, `docs/ACCOUNT_ONBOARDING.md` with 28 worked examples covering every mode × dry-run × surface, and the `/account-onboarding` skill in both trees. **OWASP: A01/A02/A03/A04/A05/A07/A08/A09 touched — 0 BLOCK.** **The Kotlin and CLI halves are compile-unverified**: the session had Java 21 only, no Gradle 9.7.0 distribution (services.gradle.org 403s through the agent proxy) and no Maven Central route. The frontend is fully verified — `npm ci`, `npm run build` and 149 unit tests green — as are the skill-sync gate and the driver's bash syntax.
- **End-of-life lifecycle management: a catalogue, a matcher that refuses to guess, owner mail and a top-10 repository ranking** — secman gains a full EOL feature: `secman eol-sync` pulls a lifecycle catalogue and re-matches every system's OS and installed products plus every imported GitHub repository's dependencies against it; `secman send-eol-notifications` mails account owners about software going EOL in the next 12 months; `/vulnerabilities/eol` answers "which software in my account / on my servers is end of life"; and ADMIN/SECCHAMPION get the top 10 repositories by distinct EOL components. **Source: endoflife.date** — public, unauthenticated, ~350 products covering both halves of this inventory (Windows/Windows Server, RHEL, Ubuntu, Debian, SLES, Amazon Linux, ESXi, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, nginx, Apache, Tomcat, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Spring Boot, Kubernetes). Microsoft's Lifecycle API was considered and rejected *as a replacement* (Microsoft-only, needs an Entra app) but is a sensible future second `sourceKey` — `EolProduct` is keyed `(source_key, product_key)` for exactly that. **The fetch runs in the backend, not the CLI**, same shape as `import-github-repos`: the host allowlist, the SSRF checks and the audit record stay in one place and the CLI host needs no egress. **The matcher never guesses** — a component whose version cannot be parsed, or whose version matches no cycle, produces no finding, because a false "end of life" on a production server lands on an owner's remediation list and costs more than a miss. Two consequences it took real care to get right: a version embedded in the name beats the version field (Windows Server reports build `10.0.17763`, which matches no cycle; the `2019` in the name does), and a cycle upstream flags EOL *without a date* is EOL with a **null** horizon, never a zero-day countdown — the owner mail promises "within N months" and must not put undated cycles in that window. Cycle resolution compares whole dot-segments, so `4.10` never matches cycle `4.1`. **Repository components are a deliberate under-approximation**: a Dependabot alert names the vulnerable *range*, never the resolved version, so the scan takes the range's upper bound — from `< 4.17.21` it knows the dependency is below 4.17.21, hence if the cycle containing 4.17.21 is already EOL then whatever is installed is in that cycle or older and is EOL too. Only `EOL` is recorded there ("approaching" says nothing about the older version in use) and an unparseable range is skipped. Findings are **replace-per-run** by `scan_run_id` with an explicit delete — `Asset` owns no cascade to `EolFinding`, because mixing cascade with manual delete-insert is what dropped 166,812 rows to 1,819 in the CrowdStrike import. Only EOL and approaching-EOL rows are stored; persisting supported ones would be a row per product per asset. **Every asset-scoped read resolves accessible asset ids first and binds them as an `IN` list**; `EolFindingRepository` has no unscoped find-all on a user-facing path, the repository ranking is ADMIN/SECCHAMPION only mirroring `GithubRepositoryController`, and an out-of-scope asset id answers 404 identically to a nonexistent one. Recipient resolution reuses `AwsAccountRecipientResolver` rather than inventing an ownership model, and addresses are rejected rather than repaired (the value is an SMTP recipient, a stored result and a log line — three sinks from one string). New: `src/backendng/…/domain/Eol*`, `EolCatalogClient/CatalogSyncService/VersionMatcher/ScanService/QueryService/NotificationService/AdminService/Writer`, `EolController`, CLI `eol-sync` + `send-eol-notifications`, `/vulnerabilities/eol`, a Lifecycle badge on `/installed-products`, `docs/EOL.md`, and the `/e2eeol` skill. **OWASP: A01/A03/A04/A05/A08/A09/A10 touched — 0 BLOCK, 35 REVIEW, all reviewed** (26 A01-sql-authz on catalogue reference-data reads and on scoped reads that take a bound `assetIds` list; 6 A03-shell-sh on quoted `curl` argv in the E2E driver; 1 A04-todo-auth on the controller's `IS_AUTHENTICATED` default, deliberate because the reads are asset-scoped and the admin verbs carry their own `@Secured`; 1 A10-outbound inside the test that asserts the SSRF guard). **Kotlin is compile-unverified** — no Gradle distribution and no Maven Central route in that session; the frontend `npm ci && npm run build` gate and the 99-test frontend unit tier are green, as is `check-skill-sync.sh`.

- **Zero-trust mobile relay: a DMZ server, secman's RBAC mirrored onto it, and an iOS app** — secman gains an outbound-only publisher (`SECMAN_RELAY_ENABLED=true`, off by default) that pushes an admin-level status snapshot to a standalone Go relay in a DMZ; the relay serves it read-only to iPhone/iPad clients and **can never reach back**. Direction is the whole design: secman dials out, the relay holds no secman credential and is never told where secman is, so a fully compromised DMZ box discloses dashboard aggregates and nothing else — no database, no write path, no lateral move. That is why a reverse proxy was rejected: a proxy needs an inbound path *and* a credential inside the DMZ. **Authorization is secman's, mirrored, not reinvented**: every snapshot section carries the roles its originating controller demands (`DashboardController`'s `@Secured("ADMIN","SECCHAMPION")` → `requiredRoles` on `kpis`), secman pushes each user's live roles as a principal record, and a read needs a matching role **and** a device scope naming the section — a scope narrows, never widens. Roles are resolved from the principal on every request and never cached on the device or baked into a token, so a demotion bites on the very next request with nothing to invalidate; principals are replace-on-push so roles can shrink, revocations stay additive so one is never undone by omission, and out-of-role / out-of-scope / nonexistent all answer an identical 403. **Sign-in layers three separate proofs**: Apple and Google ID tokens verified against their JWKS (RS256 pinned, iss/aud/exp and a single-use relay-issued nonce all checked — `aud` is what stops a token minted for another app); GitHub via the relay as a confidential OAuth client so the app never holds a GitHub credential; and a Secure Enclave P-256 key proving the device on every request. Verifying an identity grants nothing on its own — only the principal list secman pushed does. **Admins are held to a stronger bar**: a privileged role can only be bound via Apple or Google, re-checked on *every* token issue so a promotion invalidates a weakly-bound device, and the relay refuses to boot if a privileged role has no reachable strong provider. Binding is proof-of-possession throughout: the login nonce is bound to the device key and the binding request must carry that key's signature, so a captured ID token cannot register someone else's key. TLS on a selectable port in three modes — a **stdlib RFC 8555 ACME client** (Let's Encrypt, HTTP-01, renewal at 30 days), a file pair hot-reloaded on change, or plaintext for ALB termination behind an explicit `RELAY_PLAINTEXT_ACK=true`. The relay is **zero-third-party-dependency by contract** (its supply chain is the Go release plus this repo, and `go build` needs no module proxy), snapshot state is memory-only, and it fails closed on weak or placeholder secrets exactly as `JwtSigningValidator` does. 189 Go tests including a mock ACME CA that signs a real CSR and verifies every JWS, a mock OIDC issuer covering algorithm confusion / audience / issuer / expiry / nonce replay / key rotation, and end-to-end RBAC, revocation and staleness cases; a shared known-answer vector pins the ingest signature across Kotlin and Go so the two cannot drift silently. New: `src/relay/`, `com.secman.relay`, `RelayIdentity` entity, ADMIN-only `/api/relay/*`, `docs/RELAY.md`, and `extensions/secman_app_ios` (SwiftUI, iOS 26+, no third-party packages). **OWASP: A01/A02/A03/A04/A05/A07/A09/A10 touched — two A02 BLOCKs remain by design** (`RelayDigest` — SHA-256 as a message digest and over a 100-bit single-use token; BCrypt is the wrong tool there and would turn an O(1) lookup into an O(n) scan of a slow function on an unauthenticated endpoint), A10 reviewed: the outbound URL is operator config no request can influence. **The Kotlin and Swift halves are compile-unverified** — Maven Central was blocked by the egress policy, only JDK 21 was present, and there is no Swift toolchain.
- **`/secure-code` — OWASP Top 10 by construction, with a static gate that is actually tested** — `CLAUDE.md` §"OWASP Top 10 Compliance" was already binding and already good, but it is ~60 bullet points across ten categories, which is more than anyone holds in working memory while writing a controller. The predictable failure is not defiance but **partial recall**: you remember `@Secured` and forget the path id is untrusted; you bind `:name` and forget `ExcelSanitizer` on the export three files over. The new skill closes that gap in three phases. **Phase 1 routes before writing**: a 17-row table maps "does this change accept a client id / write a query / render HTML / take an upload / parse XML / make an outbound call / …" to the two or three A01–A10 categories it can actually violate and, for each, the *one existing control to reuse* — so ten categories collapse to the three that apply, and the answer is a function to call rather than a principle to remember. **Phase 2 writes with that control** (`references/controls.md`: the canonical snippet plus the file that already does it correctly, for all ten categories — `AssetFilterService`, `McpToolGuards`, bound-`:param` queries with a closed allowlist for non-bindables, `DOMPurify` at the assignment site, `ExcelSanitizer`, `ImportController.validateFile`, the `NmapParserService` XXE block, `BCryptPasswordEncoder`, `EncryptedStringConverter`, `SlackClient.validateWebhookUrl`), under three rules: reuse never re-implement, never work around a control to make something build/start/pass, deny by default. **Phase 3 verifies three ways** — the static gate, a semantic re-read against `references/blind-spots.md`, and `/security-review` when the diff touches auth, crypto, upload, export or outbound HTTP — closing with the one-line `OWASP: … touched — clean` verdict the review gate already required. **The gate is `./scripts/owasp-check.sh`**, 27 rules across A01–A10, and its design is mostly a set of decisions about *not* crying wolf. It is **diff-scoped by default** (merge-base with `origin/main`, working tree and **untracked files** included — a freshly generated controller is invisible to `git diff` and is exactly the case this exists for), with two severities: **BLOCK** for a pattern on a line this change added, **REVIEW** for a pre-existing hit in a file you touched. That split is the whole reason the gate is usable: `--all` over the repo reports 101 BLOCK and 1060 REVIEW, and a gate that is red on arrival is a gate everyone learns to ignore. Beyond the greppable rules it does three things a regex alone cannot: it resolves each new `mcp/tools/*.kt` tool name and checks `McpToolPermissions` **LISTING and CALLING separately** (counting names file-wide conflates "listed twice in LISTING" with "listed once in each", and CALLING is additionally fed by a fold over `ToolCategories.CATEGORY_PERMISSIONS`, so checking one file reported 40 of 87 tools as unregistered); it requires an `McpToolGuards` call or an equivalent `context.isAdmin` check, because a missing CALLING entry fails **closed** and looks like a bug someone will chase while a missing guard fails **open** and looks like nothing; and file-context rules (XXE block, upload validation, archive traversal) emit BLOCK only when *this* change introduced the trigger. **Precision was tuned against the real corpus rather than guessed**: the first draft reported 269 BLOCK, of which most were false. "String contains SQL keywords" matches `"Failed to send test email from account: $id"`, so injection rules now require a query-construction context (`@Query(`/`createQuery(`/`nativeQuery`/a string *starting* with SELECT) **and** an interpolation — 24 findings to 1. Naming a secret in a log message is fine (`"using the default password is insecure"`) while logging its *value* is not, so the A09 rule looks for the value reaching the call — `$password`, or a `…Password`/`…Token` identifier passed as an argument — not for the word: 119 to 6, with `len(token)` and `…Configured` explicitly excluded. `A02-secret-lit` no longer fires on `DB_PASSWORD="REDACTED"` (value starting with `$`), and `A08-upload` triggers on a `: CompletedFileUpload` parameter rather than a vestigial import. **`scripts/test/owasp-check-test.sh` is the reason any of that can be trusted.** A static gate fails in two directions and only one is visible: a false positive is loud and gets fixed, a false negative is silent — the rule quietly stops matching and the gate reports OK forever. So the self-test builds a throwaway git repo, plants a deliberately vulnerable fixture per rule, asserts the rule fires **at the right severity**, then plants the repo's *approved* pattern for the same risk (bound `:param`, `DOMPurify.sanitize`, the four XXE `setFeature` calls, `BCryptPasswordEncoder`, a logged `tokenConfigured` boolean) and asserts it stays silent — 30 assertions, all green. It has already earned its keep twice: it caught `\b` in a `file_rule` trigger, which awk does not support, silently downgrading **every** BLOCK to REVIEW and turning the gate green (portable-ERE-only is now documented at the helper), and dogfooding the gate on this very change caught it flagging its own fixtures. Fixed with an exemption that is exactly two paths — `scripts/owasp-check.sh` (it contains the patterns it hunts) and `scripts/test/owasp-check-test.sh` (it is *made of* vulnerable fixtures) — deliberately **not** "tests are exempt", since `CLAUDE.md` forbids a literal credential in "source, tests, scripts or fixtures"; the self-test asserts an ordinary test file still fires, and the exempt paths are printed on every run so the blind spot is visible rather than assumed. **Wiring**: `CLAUDE.md`'s review gate now names the command and the BLOCK/REVIEW contract; `/testsuite` runs the self-test in its fast tier (step 5, "Skill sync and the OWASP gate"); skill registered in both harness trees plus `docs/SKILLS.md`, `docs/SKILLS_AND_AGENTS.md` and `AGENTS.md` (eleven skills → twelve). **Pre-existing findings surfaced by the first audit and left unfixed deliberately** — each encodes a decision that is not this change's to make: `MemoryController` is the only controller with no `@Secured` anywhere (it serves `GET /memory`); 37 MCP tools are in `LISTING` but absent from `CALLING`, including `add_requirement`, `create_release` and `compare_releases`, which per `CLAUDE.md`'s stated rule denies `tools/call` for delegated callers, though the API-key path in `McpToolPermissionService.hasPermission` may still reach them, so the real question is whether the two-map rule or the code is authoritative; `application_register` is absent from both (already documented as intentional); and `WorkgroupAccountsModal.tsx`/`WorkgroupDomainsModal.tsx` still read `localStorage.getItem('authToken')`, dead since the JWT moved to the HttpOnly cookie but exactly the A02 anti-pattern. **OWASP: no category touched** — the change adds two offline shell scripts and Markdown, no endpoint, entity, query or data path; both new scripts are dev tooling that nothing at runtime imports. **Not verified in this environment**: `pass-cli` is unavailable and `SECMAN_HOST` is unset, so the Principle 7 gates (`/e2ejs`, `/e2evulnexception`) did not run; `./gradlew build` and `./scripts/startbackenddev.sh` (Principle 5) were not run either, as no Kotlin, TypeScript or configuration file was changed. `./scripts/check-skill-sync.sh`, `./scripts/test/owasp-check-test.sh` (30/30) and `./scripts/owasp-check.sh` on this branch all pass.
- **AWS account risk assessment: validation pass, three defects closed** — a review of the opt-in auto-start path (`manage-user-mappings import --start-risk-assessment --risk-usecase <name>`, mirrored on `import-s3`, REST `POST /api/user-mappings/bulk` and MCP `import_user_mappings`) confirmed the contract holds — the flag is off by default, the use case comes from a flag, and without the flag the import runs exactly as before — and turned up three things that did not. **(1) The deadline had no upper bound.** `validateStartRequest` rejected `< 1` and nothing else, so `--risk-deadline-days 2147483647` produced an `endDate` outside the SQL `DATE` range; because assessments are started *after* the mapping import commits, that surfaced as a per-account error with the mappings already persisted, and a merely absurd value like `100000` (one keystroke from `1000`) was accepted silently into an assessment the reminder scheduler — which looks two days ahead — would never wake up for. Now `MAX_DEADLINE_DAYS = 3650`, checked in `validateStartRequest` so REST and MCP share it, mirrored as `UserMappingCliService.MAX_RISK_DEADLINE_DAYS` in both CLI commands (the CLI is a separate Gradle module and cannot reference the backend constant; `ImportCommandTest` pins the two together), and clamped rather than thrown in `startAssessmentsForNewAccounts` for a direct service call, since that runs past the commit point. The MCP input schema now advertises `maximum`. **(2) The idempotent skip was reported as a failure.** When a pair already had an open assessment, `createAssessment` returned "an open risk assessment (id=…) already exists" in `AccountRiskAssessmentInfo.error`, so both CLI commands printed it as ❌/FAILED, counted it in `riskAssessmentFailures` and exited 1 — for an outcome that is the feature working correctly. The DTO gained `skipped` / `skipReason` (and the MCP result the same two fields), `error` stays null, and both CLIs render it as a skip that does not affect the exit code. **Load-bearing detail:** the owner-notification gate used to rely on `error != null` to suppress the duplicate mail, so it now tests `!info.skipped` as well — otherwise every re-import would re-notify. The path is only reachable when the mapping row was deleted and the account is imported again while its assessment is still open; a plain re-import never reaches the guard, because the account is no longer new. **(3) The email boundary was too loose.** `UserMappingService.emailRegex` was `^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$`, and `[^@]` matches control characters, spaces and commas — so `alice\r\nBcc: x@evil.com` passed validation. That address is not just a row: it becomes the SMTP recipient of the start and reminder mails, it is interpolated into log lines (`Started risk assessment … owner={}`), and it is written into the assessment's `notes`. The pattern now excludes whitespace and `, ; : < > " \` (a comma makes `InternetAddress.parse` split one recipient into two; a CR/LF reaches a log line), length is capped at the 255-char column width so an overlong address fails as one ordinary row error instead of a post-commit `DataException`, and the three "invalid …" messages that echo the rejected value run it through `sanitizeForMessage` (control characters → `?`, truncated at 80). The same pattern went into `UserMappingBulkImportService`'s `notifyAddress` copy and the CLI's `UserMappingValidator`. Also: `import-s3` now emits the "`--risk-usecase` is ignored because `--start-risk-assessment` is not set" warning `import` already had — silently ignoring it is how an operator ends up believing assessments ran. **Test skill.** `/aws-account-risk-assessment` (driver `scripts/test/test-e2e-aws-account-risk-assessment.sh`) gained three phases: the opt-in default (import a new account with no flag → mapping created, no assessment, no `AWS_ACCOUNT` asset; and the ignored-use-case warning), the deadline bound on both CLI and MCP, and a reworked idempotency phase that actually reaches the guard — it deletes the mapping so the account is new again while the assessment stays open, then asserts exit 0, a "skipped" line, no ❌, and still exactly one tracked assessment. Its **cleanup was also unsafe**: it deleted every risk assessment whose notes contained the substring `886` or `887`, which on a real environment means any assessment for a genuine AWS account whose id contains those digits. It now matches the owner-email prefix the service writes into the notes (`owner: e2e-awsra-`), which is both exact and stable across runs, sweeps mappings by that same prefix instead of this run's two timestamped ids (so earlier interrupted runs are cleaned up too), and finally removes the `AWS_ACCOUNT` basis assets — which nothing removed before, so every run leaked one. Accounts are now one per phase in a fixed `88[4-9]<stamp>000` shape, which is what the asset sweep matches. **Not verified in this session:** the environment had no Gradle distribution and no route to Maven Central, so the Kotlin changes are compile-unverified and neither the unit tests nor the E2E gates were run.
- **Generic chat notifications (Slack + Telegram), configurable per user** — SecMan can now message a user in Slack and/or Telegram when a reportable event completes, with each user choosing their own destination and, independently per channel, which events they want. Two events ship: `CROWDSTRIKE_REPORT_COMPLETED` ("New CrowdStrike report completed") and `AWS_ACCOUNT_IMPORT_COMPLETED` ("New AWS account import completed"). **Architecture is transport- and event-agnostic on purpose.** Publishers know nothing about chat: they publish a `ChatNotificationEvent` (event type, title, summary, label/value fields) and `ChatNotificationEventListener` (`@EventListener @Async`) hands it to `ChatNotificationService`, which resolves subscribers, destinations and rendering. Adding a reportable event is a `NotificationEventType` constant plus one publish call — the settings APIs, both settings UIs and the dispatcher all derive from the enum, so nothing else changes. Adding a transport is one client plus one branch, with no publisher touched. **Subscriptions are rows, not columns**: `user_notification_subscription (user_id, channel, event_type)` — so a new event type or a whole new channel costs no migration, "who wants X over Slack" is a single indexed lookup on the dispatch path, and one user can route CrowdStrike to Slack and AWS imports to Telegram. Saving one channel's settings never disturbs the other's subscriptions (the replace is a per-channel diff, which also preserves `created_at` on kept rows). **Destination resolution.** Slack: personal incoming webhook → the user's channel via the workspace bot → the workspace default channel. Telegram: the user's chat ID is always required (Telegram addresses a conversation, not a person), with the token being the user's personal bot if set, otherwise the workspace bot — so a personal bot keeps working even when workspace delivery is switched off. A subscriber who is enabled but has nowhere to send is recorded as `SKIPPED`, not `FAILED`; the UI resolves the same precedence client-side (`resolveSlackDestination` / `resolveTelegramDestination`) and warns *before* save rather than letting someone tick boxes that silently deliver nothing. **Where the events fire.** AWS account imports complete in one call, so `UserMappingBulkImportService.execute` (REST bulk + MCP, tagged with the calling entry point) and both `ImportController` upload paths publish immediately, after the import has committed and last among the post-commit side effects. CrowdStrike has no such point: a full CLI import arrives as ~94 sub-batch requests across 3 concurrent workers with no well-defined last batch, so `ImportCompletionNotifier` accumulates the run's totals in memory and a `@Scheduled` sweep publishes exactly **one** event once `SECMAN_CHAT_CROWDSTRIKE_QUIET_PERIOD_SECONDS` (180s) have passed with no activity — the same server-side debounce shape, and for the same reason, as `MaterializedViewRefreshService.requestDeferredRefresh`, and it keeps working for older CLI versions, the `/api/crowdstrike/vulnerabilities/save` path and manual callers. **Security.** The per-user Slack webhook URL is the only place in the platform where a non-admin supplies a URL the backend then fetches, so it is checked against a fixed `https://hooks.slack.com/` prefix *and* parsed-host equality (a prefix match alone passes `https://hooks.slack.com.evil.example/...`), rejects userinfo, non-default ports and non-https, and redirects are never followed. The Telegram bot token is interpolated into the request URL **path** (`/bot<token>/sendMessage`), so its `<digits>:<secret>` shape is validated as a security control — a token containing `/` or `..` would otherwise redirect the request to another path on the API host. Slack channels and Telegram chat IDs are validated against conservative character classes. Every credential (both workspace bot tokens, each user's webhook URL and personal bot token) is stored through `EncryptedStringConverter`, never returned by any API — the responses report only `…Configured: true/false` — and the `***HIDDEN***` mask is accepted back to mean "keep the stored value", with `''` meaning "clear it". Slack messages escape Slack's three reserved characters so an imported hostname cannot inject a fake link; Telegram messages are sent with **no** `parse_mode`, deliberately, because MarkdownV2 reserves 18 characters and rejects the whole message on one unescaped occurrence. Every route acts on the caller's own settings — the user id comes from the token and is never read from the body. Dispatch is deliberately **not** `@Transactional`: it performs outbound HTTP with a multi-second timeout per recipient, and wrapping it would pin a pooled DB connection for the whole fan-out (the 2026-07-21 HikariCP starvation incident was exactly that shape). Delivery is per-recipient and per-channel isolated: one bad webhook never stops another user's message, one channel's outage never suppresses the other, and nothing can propagate back into the import that published the event. **New endpoints**: `GET /api/notification-events` (catalogue, authenticated); `GET/PUT /api/slack/settings`, `POST /api/slack/settings/test`, `GET/PUT /api/telegram/settings`, `POST /api/telegram/settings/test` (authenticated, self-scoped); `GET/PUT /api/slack/config`, `POST /api/slack/config/test`, `GET/PUT /api/telegram/config` (ADMIN). No Telegram workspace test endpoint — a bot token addresses no conversation on its own, so a meaningful test needs a chat ID and lives on the user page. **UI**: `/chat-notifications` (all users, linked from the account dropdown) with independent Slack and Telegram cards sharing a `NotificationEventSelector` and `ChatDeliveryStatusLine`; `/admin/chat-config` (ADMIN, linked under System Configuration). **Schema**: `V252__chat_notifications.sql` adds `slack_config`, `telegram_config`, `user_slack_settings`, `user_telegram_settings`, `user_notification_subscription`. **Tests**: `SlackClientTest` and `TelegramClientTest` (the URL/token/channel/chat-id allowlists, including that a rejected value never reaches the network), `ChatMessageRendererTest` (both flavours + Slack escaping), `ChatNotificationServiceTest` (24 cases: subscription filtering, both destination precedence chains, skipped-vs-failed, per-recipient and per-channel isolation, outcome recording), `ImportCompletionNotifierTest` (94 sub-batches → one event with correct totals, nothing published mid-import, totals reset between runs, the account-ID list cap), and `chatValidation.test.ts` on the frontend (17 cases mirroring the backend validators and both destination resolvers). On merging main, the newly-binding §OWASP Top 10 section prompted a re-read of the diff against A01–A10 and turned up one real gap: provider exception text was logged and persisted into `last_delivery_error` verbatim, and several JDK `HttpClient` exceptions echo the request URI — which for Telegram *contains the bot token* and for a Slack webhook *is* the credential. Both clients now scrub the secret out of any error before it is logged or stored (A02: no credential may reach a value that lands in a log), covered by a test per client. Migration renumbered `V251` → `V252__chat_notifications.sql`, since main landed its own `V251__user_profile_picture.sql` — two files sharing a Flyway version fails the migration at boot. **OWASP: A01/A02/A03/A04/A05/A08/A09/A10 touched — clean.** **Not verified in this environment**: `./gradlew build` and `./scripts/startbackenddev.sh` could not run — the session's egress policy blocks `services.gradle.org` and `repo1.maven.org`, and no Gradle 9.7.0 distribution or dependency cache is present — so the backend is compile-unverified and CLAUDE.md principle 5 and the principle-7 E2E gates are undischarged. The frontend gates did run: `npm ci && npm run build` clean, `npm test` 76 passing, and `@astrojs/check` reports zero type errors in any new or changed file (the 10 it finds are all pre-existing in untouched files).

- **Profile picture management (upload / crop / replace / remove)** — any authenticated user can now set an avatar from `/profile`; it replaces the generic `bi-person-circle` icon beside their name in the header dropdown. Scope is deliberately **own picture only** — there are no ADMIN-manages-others endpoints, and none of the three routes (`GET`/`POST`/`DELETE /api/users/profile/picture`, all on the existing `UserProfileController`) takes a user identifier, so the subject is always `authentication.name` and cross-user access is *structurally* impossible rather than merely checked. The paths are two literal segments, so they cannot collide with the ADMIN-gated single-segment `@Get("/{id}")` on `UserController`, which shares the `/api/users` prefix. **Bytes are stored in the database but never as uploaded**: `ProfilePictureService` validates cheapest-first (size cap → MIME allowlist → filename-extension/MIME agreement → magic bytes → header-only dimensions → the `ImageReader`'s own `formatName`) and then decodes, centre-crops to a square, scales to 256 px and re-encodes. That round trip — not the magic-byte sniff — is the control that actually matters: it destroys polyglot payloads (a valid PNG with `<script>` appended still decodes as a PNG and would pass any header check) and strips EXIF/GPS metadata, verified by a dedicated test. The **dimension probe runs before `reader.read(0)`**, so a 2 MB PNG cannot decode into a multi-gigabyte `BufferedImage` and trip `-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError` on the 1 GB heap; without that guard the endpoint would be a single-request kill switch. WEBP is deliberately **absent** from the allowlist (the JDK has no WEBP reader, so accepting it would mean storing bytes that were never decoded) — this costs nothing in practice because the frontend cropper exports its canvas as PNG, so WEBP/HEIC sources still work end to end. SVG is rejected three independent ways: not in the allowlist, `.svg` already in `SecurityService.DANGEROUS_EXTENSIONS`, and no SVG `ImageReader` exists. Only the JDK is used (`javax.imageio`/`java.awt.image`); `-Djava.awt.headless=true` was pinned in `applicationDefaultJvmArgs`. Storage is a **side table** `user_profile_picture` (V251, 1:1, `ON DELETE CASCADE`), not a column on `users`: `users` is loaded on every authenticated request and **`@Basic(fetch = LAZY)` on a `@Lob` is inert without Hibernate bytecode enhancement, which this build does not enable** — a blob column on `users` would therefore be fetched eagerly, every time. For the same reason the hot metadata paths use the blob-free projection `findUpdatedAtByUserId`, never `findByUserId`. `UserProfileDto` and `AuthController.StatusResponse` gained `hasProfilePicture` + `profilePictureUpdatedAt` (both defaulted, so purely additive); `LoginResponse` and the four `sessionStorage['user']` writers were deliberately **left alone** — `auth-init.ts` and `login/success.astro` store the whole `/api/auth/status` response verbatim and `Login.tsx` redirects immediately into a fresh status call, so they pick the fields up for free. **The header `<img>` is gated on `hasProfilePicture` rather than rendered unconditionally with an `onError` fallback**: `tests/js-error-scanner.mjs` records any status ≥ 400 as a failure, so an unconditional request would 404 on every page for every user without a picture and fail the `/e2ejs` merge gate. For the same reason `DELETE` returns 204 unconditionally instead of 404 when nothing is set. Frontend: new `ProfilePictureCard.tsx` (preview, drag & drop, and a hand-rolled canvas crop/zoom step — pointer-drag to pan, wheel/slider to zoom, exported at 512 px via `canvas.toBlob`; no cropping library added, the repo carries none), mounted as the first card on `/profile` and seeded from the profile fetch that already ran, so no extra metadata request. After a save or removal it patches `window.currentUser`/`sessionStorage` and re-dispatches the **existing** `userLoaded` event that `Header.tsx` already listens for, so the navbar avatar updates without a reload. Serving uses `inline` disposition — the first such endpoint in the repo — which is safe only because the `Content-Type` served is the stored, service-chosen value and never the client's declared one, and the `Content-Disposition` filename is synthesized from a `Long` and a constant so no user input reaches a response header. Upload, removal **and rejection** are audit-logged (a stream of `PROFILE_PICTURE_UPLOAD_REJECTED` is exactly the signal wanted when someone probes with polyglots). Tests: `ProfilePictureServiceTest` (19 cases incl. the polyglot-stripping and bomb-guard proofs), `UserProfilePictureIntegrationTest` (happy path, replace-updates-one-row, every rejection branch, 401 on all three routes, idempotent delete, cross-user isolation, cascade). Docs: `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md` (`SECMAN_PROFILE_PICTURE_*`).

- **Skill sync between Claude Code and Codex is now a two-way obligation, defined for both harnesses** — the repo keeps every skill twice, in `.claude/skills/` (loaded by Claude Code) and `.agents/skills/` (loaded by Codex and other `AGENTS.md`-driven agents). The rule covering them was written only from the Claude side: CLAUDE.md said "*whenever a `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` file is edited*, the matching `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` must be updated in the same change", `AGENTS.md` — the only file Codex reads — said **nothing about skills at all**, and the per-file banner (present in the `.agents/` copies only) ended with "never let this file diverge *ahead of* the Claude Code version". Read literally, a Codex session editing its own tree was under no stated obligation to touch the Claude tree, and the agent that most needed the rule never saw it. The OS string is stored in the existing `vulnerability_exception.scope_value` column — **no DB migration** (`scope` is already `VARCHAR(20)`). Recipients are deduplicated case-insensitively; an account with zero recipients across all three paths is reported as unmapped. The notification body text is read from a file supplied via `--file`/`-f` (mandatory) — operators customise the message without redeploying. The account list is always appended below the custom text. New `NewAccountNotificationService` follows the same pattern as `UserVulnerabilityNotificationService`. Backend endpoint: `POST /api/cli/new-account-notifications/send` (ADMIN). Docs: `docs/CLI.md`.

Reuses `UserVulnerabilityNotificationService.sendUserVulnerabilityNotifications` (new `emailPrefix` recipient filter — case-insensitive `startsWith`, applied after AWS-account→user mapping) and the existing `POST /api/cli/user-vulnerability-notifications/send` endpoint (new optional `emailPrefix` field). MCP tool is ADMIN-only via delegation, permission `NOTIFICATIONS_SEND`. E2E coverage: Phase 8b in `scripts/test/test-e2e-vuln-exception-full.sh` (dry-run + missing-arg + non-admin negatives). Docs: `docs/CLI.md`, `docs/MCP.md`.

ADMIN and SECCHAMPION users (the assessment's assessor or requestor; ADMIN can act on any) can trigger an OpenRouter LLM to pre-fill compliance answers as draft `Response` rows with confidence + citations. Human always reviews and submits.
  - DB-backed master switch on `app_settings.ai_risk_assessment_enabled` (V216), flippable by ADMIN at `/appsettings`. Env var `AI_RISK_ASSESSMENT_ENABLED` only seeds the default at first create — once a row exists, the DB column is authoritative. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` resolved via `pass-cli` is still required for the feature to actually call out. The UI "AI Pre-fill" button is gated on `GET /api/ai-risk-assessment/status` so it stays hidden when the switch is off.
  - Per-job hard cost cap `secman.ai.risk-assessment.max-cost-per-job-usd` (default 5 USD) plus global concurrency cap `max-concurrent-jobs-global` (default 2). Pre-flight rejects over-budget runs; mid-flight aborts and marks `FAILED`, retaining partial successes.

  - Confidence band derivation: `score = 0.5·self_reported + 0.3·min(valid_citations, 3)/3 + 0.2·answer_is_not_UNKNOWN`. HIGH requires ≥1 valid citation (downgrade rule). Stored both raw + band so thresholds can retune without re-running the model.
  - Redaction (NFR-4): `PromptBuilder.redact()` scrubs emails, IPv4 addresses, and `*.internal/*.local/*.corp/*.lan/*.intranet` URLs from the prompt regardless of caller hygiene. Locked by `PromptBuilderTest`.
  - Re-run safety: `startJob` excludes `source = AI_EDITED` rows unless `force = true`. `clear-low-confidence` only touches `AI_GENERATED` rows whose linked suggestion has `confidenceBand = LOW`.
  - Mirrors `TranslationService` (JDK HttpClient + dedicated `ai` executor + Caffeine 24h cache) and `ExportJobService` (DB-backed job, IO executor, heartbeat, scheduled stale-job reclaim).
  - Docs: `docs/AI_RISK_ASSESSMENT.md`; spec/plan/tasks under `specs/088-ai-risk-assessment-answers/`.

Root cause from the prod log: the CLI's cutoff arrived timezone-skewed (>1h in the backend's future), the old guard fell back to `backendNow − 30min`, and because the import ran longer than 30 minutes the sweep judged everything the run imported in its first half-hour "stale" and deleted it — 727,637 rows in one statement, aborted=false. Fixes, layered: (1) **cutoff translation** — the CLI now sends `clientNow`; the backend measures the clock offset and translates `importStartedAt` into its own clock, and without `clientNow` a future cutoff **aborts** the sweep (delete nothing) instead of guessing; (2) **failure-aware sweep scope** — hosts whose Falcon Stage-2 batch failed/was truncated (`StreamingImportResult.failedHosts`) or whose backend POST/per-server transaction failed (`BatchStorageResult.failedHostnames`, `ImportStatisticsDto.failedHostnames`) are excluded from `queriedHosts`, since their un-refreshed rows were never fetched, not remediated; (3) **percentage brake** `CROWDSTRIKE_RECONCILE_MAX_DELETE_PERCENT` (default 20, 100 disables) over the resolved scope, fail-CLOSED on count errors — the zero-refresh brake only catches fully-empty runs; (4) **scoped per-host replace** — `importVulnerabilitiesForServer` no longer wipes every row on the asset: it deletes `source=CROWDSTRIKE` rows at the batch's `runSeverities` (new optional DTO field; source-only fallback for old callers), so MEDIUM/LOW and XLSX/nmap/manual rows survive, and a batch whose rows are ALL filtered out (blank CVE / missing patch date) skips the delete instead of committing delete-without-reinsert; (5) **stale-asset cleanup correctness** — rule A now vetoes assets with a recent `crowdStrikeAgentSeenAt` (a fully-patched host with a live sensor never refreshes `crowdStrikeLastImportedAt`), brake numerator and deletion use one shared cutoff and the same query, and the brake fails closed when the tracked-asset count is unavailable; (6) **observability** — reconcile audit columns on `crowdstrike_reconcile_job` (V257: queried/resolved/excluded counts, stale candidates, refreshed, dry_run), `--reconcile-dry-run` CLI flag, per-host replace logging at INFO, a `CROWDSTRIKE_RECONCILE_ABORTED` chat-notification event, and the MV refresh `triggered_by` insert no longer dies on over-length reasons (`.take(50)`, the log's second error). `scripts/import.sh` `--last-seen-days` regression 1→30 fixed (comment already said 30). `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md` §CrowdStrike reconcile sweep.
+- **Apple `container` database selection (`--db`)** — `secman-container.sh up` now takes `--db container|host|none` (plus `--db-host/--db-port/--db-name`; `--with-db`/`--no-db` are aliases for the first and last). `container`, the default, runs the in-container MariaDB and publishes it on :3306; `host` runs none and points the stack at the MariaDB already installed on the Mac; `none` leaves `DB_CONNECT` to `pass-cli`. `host` was previously not reachable at all: the egress policy carries only 80/443/22 to allow-set addresses, so port 3306 to the Mac was refused with no rule capable of permitting it. The entrypoint now settles the mode **before** the firewall is built, resolves the Mac's address (it is the container's default gateway, which only the container can see), and writes the result to `/run/secman-dev/db/env` — the single file the firewall, `devctl` and every login shell read, so the iptables rule and the JDBC URL cannot disagree, including after a `refresh-egress` that inherits none of the entrypoint's environment. The rule is deliberately narrow: one address, one port, outside the allow-set (which is only ever matched on 80/443/22), and the address must be private — a public one is refused unless `SECMAN_DEV_DB_ALLOW_PUBLIC=1`, so a convenience flag cannot become general 3306 egress. The choice is made effective rather than advisory: `/etc/profile.d/secman-dev.sh` exports the resulting `DB_CONNECT` (plus the throwaway `DB_USERNAME`/`DB_PASSWORD` in `container` mode only), and `scripts/startbackenddev.sh` now honours a preset `DB_CONNECT` and falls back to `pass://Test/SECMAN/DB_CONNECT` when it is unset — unchanged behaviour on a Mac. `devctl db status` / `secman-container.sh db` report the mode, the URL and a live reachability probe, and name the three silent failure modes of `--db host` in order (server not running, bound to 127.0.0.1 only, no grant for the container's subnet); `devctl db start` refuses outside `container` mode rather than raising a second server behind a URL that names a different one. Every value that reaches an iptables rule or a JDBC URL goes through a closed character allowlist at both ends (§A03). `docs/APPLE_CONTAINER_DEV.md` §Choosing the database.

Suffixed variants such as `aws-DevOps-x-rolegreen` are deliberately not matched — a fuzzy rule here would hand an unrelated workgroup's members access to an account's assets, since a link is unified-asset-access **rule #9** (`WorkgroupAwsAccount`), not bookkeeping. source-only fallback for old callers), so MEDIUM/LOW and XLSX/nmap/manual rows survive, and a batch whose rows are ALL filtered out (blank CVE / missing patch date) skips the delete instead of committing delete-without-reinsert; (5) **stale-asset cleanup correctness** — rule A now vetoes assets with a recent `crowdStrikeAgentSeenAt` (a fully-patched host with a live sensor never refreshes `crowdStrikeLastImportedAt`), brake numerator and deletion use one shared cutoff and the same query, and the brake fails closed when the tracked-asset count is unavailable; (6) **observability** — reconcile audit columns on `crowdstrike_reconcile_job` (V257: queried/resolved/excluded counts, stale candidates, refreshed, dry_run), `--reconcile-dry-run` CLI flag, per-host replace logging at INFO, a `CROWDSTRIKE_RECONCILE_ABORTED` chat-notification event, and the MV refresh `triggered_by` insert no longer dies on over-length reasons (`.take(50)`, the log's second error). `scripts/import.sh` `--last-seen-days` regression 1→30 fixed (comment already said 30). `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md` §CrowdStrike reconcile sweep.
+- **Apple `container` database selection (`--db`)** — `secman-container.sh up` now takes `--db container|host|none` (plus `--db-host/--db-port/--db-name`; `--with-db`/`--no-db` are aliases for the first and last). `container`, the default, runs the in-container MariaDB and publishes it on :3306; `host` runs none and points the stack at the MariaDB already installed on the Mac; `none` leaves `DB_CONNECT` to `pass-cli`. `host` was previously not reachable at all: the egress policy carries only 80/443/22 to allow-set addresses, so port 3306 to the Mac was refused with no rule capable of permitting it. The entrypoint now settles the mode **before** the firewall is built, resolves the Mac's address (it is the container's default gateway, which only the container can see), and writes the result to `/run/secman-dev/db/env` — the single file the firewall, `devctl` and every login shell read, so the iptables rule and the JDBC URL cannot disagree, including after a `refresh-egress` that inherits none of the entrypoint's environment. The rule is deliberately narrow: one address, one port, outside the allow-set (which is only ever matched on 80/443/22), and the address must be private — a public one is refused unless `SECMAN_DEV_DB_ALLOW_PUBLIC=1`, so a convenience flag cannot become general 3306 egress. The choice is made effective rather than advisory: `/etc/profile.d/secman-dev.sh` exports the resulting `DB_CONNECT` (plus the throwaway `DB_USERNAME`/`DB_PASSWORD` in `container` mode only), and `scripts/startbackenddev.sh` now honours a preset `DB_CONNECT` and falls back to `pass://Test/SECMAN/DB_CONNECT` when it is unset — unchanged behaviour on a Mac. `devctl db status` / `secman-container.sh db` report the mode, the URL and a live reachability probe, and name the three silent failure modes of `--db host` in order (server not running, bound to 127.0.0.1 only, no grant for the container's subnet); `devctl db start` refuses outside `container` mode rather than raising a second server behind a URL that names a different one. Every value that reaches an iptables rule or a JDBC URL goes through a closed character allowlist at both ends (§A03). `docs/APPLE_CONTAINER_DEV.md` §Choosing the database.

1	# Claude Code Agent Context
     2	
     3	Security requirement, vulnerability and risk management platform.
     4	
     5	## Stack
     6	
     7	- Backend: Kotlin 2.4.20 / Java 25, Micronaut 5.2, Hibernate JPA → `src/backendng/`
     8	- Frontend: Astro 7.3 + React 19 islands, Axios, JWT in the HttpOnly `secman_auth` cookie → `src/frontend/`
     9	- CLI: Kotlin + Picocli 4.7.7, AWS SDK v2 → `src/cli/`
    10	- Mobile relay: Go 1.24, **zero third-party dependencies** (stdlib only, incl. its own RFC 8555 ACME client) → `src/relay/`
    11	- DB: MariaDB 11.4, Flyway + Hibernate auto-migration
    12	- Build: Gradle 9.8.0 (Kotlin DSL)
    13	- MCP: Streamable HTTP / JSON-RPC 2.0. `X-MCP-User-Email` header is **mandatory** on `tools/list` and `tools/call` (only `initialize` and `ping` exempt).
    14	
    15	## Roles (RBAC)
   235	a new event or channel needs no migration and per-channel saves never disturb each other.
   236	Dispatch must stay non-`@Transactional` — it does per-recipient HTTP with a multi-second timeout.
   237	**Security**: the per-user Slack webhook URL is the only user-supplied URL the backend fetches —
   238	host-allowlisted in `SlackClient.validateWebhookUrl`, redirects never followed. The Telegram bot
   239	token goes in the request URL *path*, so `TelegramClient.validateBotToken` is a security control,
   240	not input hygiene. All credentials use `EncryptedStringConverter`, are never returned (only
   241	`…Configured` booleans), and accept `***HIDDEN***` back to mean "keep". Telegram sends with no
   242	`parse_mode` on purpose. CrowdStrike completion is detected by a quiet-period debounce in
   243	`ImportCompletionNotifier` (no last batch exists), AWS account imports publish inline post-commit.
   244	
   245	### Transactional replace (CrowdStrike vuln import)
   246	Per server: `findOrCreateAsset` → `vulnerabilityRepository.deleteByAssetId()` → `saveAll`, all in one `@Transactional`. Idempotent; missing CVEs in the next import = remediation.
   247	
   248	**CRITICAL**: `Asset.vulnerabilities` MUST NOT use `cascade=ALL` or `orphanRemoval=true`. JPA cascade fights the manual delete-insert and silently drops 99% of rows (real incident: 166,812 → 1,819). Use explicit `vulnerabilityRepository.deleteByAssetId()` in the service. See `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md`.
   249	
   250	## Test Infrastructure
   251	
   252	JUnit 6, Mockk, AssertJ, `@MicronautTest`. Integration tests run against an **external MariaDB** (no Docker/Testcontainers). **`junit-jupiter-params` is not on the classpath** — `@ParameterizedTest` will not compile; loop inside a plain `@Test`. Helpers in `src/backendng/src/test/kotlin/com/secman/testutil/`:
   253	- `BaseIntegrationTest` — base for DB-backed tests; datasource comes from `application-test.yml`.
   254	- `TestDataFactory` — admin/vuln/regular user, asset, vulnerability builders.
   255	- `TestAuthHelper` — JWT login → bearer token.
   256	
   257	Run backend tests through `./scripts/runbackendtests.sh` or wrap Gradle with `./scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh --database-only --`. The runner creates and owns a fresh MariaDB schema, sets `TEST_DB_*`, and removes it after the run. Direct Gradle tests without its ownership marker fail before execution.
   258	
   259	```kotlin
   260	class MyIntegrationTest : BaseIntegrationTest() { @Inject lateinit var repo: Repository }
   261	```
   262	
   263	**Frontend unit tier**: `cd src/frontend && npm test` — Node's own runner with native
   264	TypeScript stripping, no test-framework dependency. Tests live beside their module as
   265	`<module>.test.ts`. Imports resolve `.ts` only: Node cannot parse JSX, so pure logic
   266	must be extracted out of `.tsx` into a sibling `.ts` module to be unit-testable (the
   267	resolver hook in `src/frontend/test/` handles extensionless specifiers and raises a
   268	pointed error on `.tsx`). Details in `docs/TESTING.md` §Frontend.
   269	
   270	No persistent `secman_test` setup is needed. Existing application rows are never test input or cleanup targets.
   271	
   272	## File Layout
   273	
   274	`src/backendng/…/com/secman/{domain,controller,service,repository,config,dto,filter,mcp,relay}/` · `src/frontend/src/{pages,components,services,layouts}/` · `src/cli/…/com/secman/cli/{commands,service}/` · `src/shared/…/com/secman/crowdstrike/{client,dto,auth,model}/` (Gradle subproject shared by backendng + cli) · `src/relay/{cmd,internal,deploy}/` (Go). `application.yml` + `email-templates/` under `src/backendng/src/main/resources/`. Env: `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`. Full tree: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §File layout.
   275	
   276	## Extension Clients (`extensions/`)
   277	
   278	`secman_ai_github`, `secman_web_check`, and `secman_intra_mon` are independent Python repositories with their own remotes, **gitignored here** — root `git status` never shows them. Normal builds do not cover them. The first two share the version-1 result contract covered by `/integration-contract-test` and `scripts/check-integration-contract.sh --run`; `secman_intra_mon` uses the legacy REST surface and needs the same manual five-dimension contract check described below. `secman_source` is a separate gitignored local source-review CLI with its own remote; it calls neither SecMan nor the relay, so it has no backend or relay contract to check here.
   279	
   280	`secman_app_ios` (iOS/iPadOS status app, Swift) is a **relay client, not a backend client**: it never calls `/api/…` and holds no secman credential. A change to a secman endpoint cannot break it. What *can* is the relay contract — `com.secman.relay.RelayDtos`, the section names and `SECTION_POLICIES` in `RelaySnapshotBuilder`, or `src/relay/internal/api`. Both envelopes carry a `schemaVersion` for that reason; bump it on a breaking change and update `relaySupportedSnapshotSchemaVersion` in the app. Sweep its surface with `grep -rnE '/api/v1/|/ingest/v1/' extensions/secman_app_ios --include='*.swift'`.
   281	
   282	Always rediscover the surface; a written list means a newly added call gets checked by nobody:
   283	```bash
   284	grep -rnE '/api/|"/mcp"|X-MCP-User-Email' extensions --include='*.py' --exclude-dir=.venv
   285	```
   286	As of 2026-09-30: legacy calls remain `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/vulnerabilities/cli-add`, `PUT /api/assets/import`, and `POST /api/scan/upload-nmap`. Version 1 uses `GET /api/integrations/v1/scanners/{id}/subjects` and `POST /api/integrations/v1/runs`; see `docs/INTEGRATION_RESULTS.md`.
   287	
   288	When you change any of those endpoints, verify all five dimensions against the client: **path, HTTP method, request field names, response fields the client reads, and `@Secured` roles / required headers**. Field names matter most — Jackson drops unknown keys without error, so a rename makes the client "succeed" while sending nothing. Update the client's `tests/` too; a test asserting the old shape is drift.
   289	
   290	Fix and commit **inside the extension repo, path-scoped** (`git -C extensions/<repo> commit -m "…" -- <files>`) so pre-existing dirty files are not swallowed. Never `git add -A` / `commit -a`, and **never push** — those repos have their own review. An `@Secured` tightening is a *report*, not a fix: you cannot see which roles the client's service account holds.
   291	
   292	## E2E Runner
   293	
   294	**Database safety:** Database-mutating test drivers must be invoked through
   295	`./scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh -- <driver and arguments>`. It creates a
   296	marked disposable schema and restricted database user, copies schema structure
   297	and Flyway history but no application rows, and starts a separate stack on
   298	18080/14321. It cleans verified abandoned test schemas before a new run and
   299	removes its own schema on exit. Direct driver calls fail closed. Do not delete
   300	an unverified legacy fixture merely because its name matches a test prefix.
   301	The normal 8080/4321 cold-start and stop rules below apply to read-only skills;
   302	the isolated runner owns the lifecycle for mutating skills.
   303	
   304	Triggered by `/e2eexception`, `/admin-asset-e2e`, `/e2ejs`, `/e2evulnexception`, `/e2eeol`, `/account-onboarding`, `/aws-account-workgroup-import`, `/importtest`, `/crowdstrike-vuln-match` skills.
   305	
   306	- **Cold start for read-only skills**: stop the regular backend/frontend via the canonical stop scripts before restarting them. Database-mutating skills never stop or reuse that stack; the isolated runner starts and stops its own services.
   307	- Backend changes (Kotlin/Java) → restart required.
   308	- Frontend changes → Vite hot-reload (no restart).
   309	- Config (`astro.config.mjs`, `application.yml`) → restart.
   310	- Logs: `.e2e-logs/` (gitignored). Max 5 fix iterations.
   311	- **Liveness check is port-bind**, not HTTP: `lsof -iTCP:8080 -sTCP:LISTEN -n -P` (120s budget) and `:4321` (60s budget).
   312	- **Functional checks** use `SECMAN_HOST` for the regular stack or the runner-provided test-only URLs for isolated E2E. Never target regular 8080/4321 for a mutating test.
   313	
   314	---
   315	
   316	*Last updated: 2026-10-04*
   317

   319	
   320	Summaries of the three newest only. Every entry is written **verbatim** to `docs/CHANGELOG.md` when it happens — grep there for the full detail.

   322	- **MCP vulnerability query E2E regression (2026-09-27)** — the automatically discovered Playwright suite now verifies MCP discovery, severity-array schema, filtering, pagination, hydrated asset names, and delegated non-admin authorization on both HTTP transports. It uses only disposable-runner data and generated API keys. See `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.
   323	
   324	- **Guest invitation E2E regression (2026-09-27)** — `assessment-guest-invitation.spec.ts` now proves loopback delivery plus anonymous questionnaire load, save, reload, and submit. The public page uses the current token-bound response contract and does not mount the login-only attachment widget. See `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.

Migration V282 preserves legacy values while allowing current token creation to deliver external respondent notifications. See `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.

   235	a new event or channel needs no migration and per-channel saves never disturb each other.
   236	Dispatch must stay non-`@Transactional` — it does per-recipient HTTP with a multi-second timeout.
   237	**Security**: the per-user Slack webhook URL is the only user-supplied URL the backend fetches —
   238	host-allowlisted in `SlackClient.validateWebhookUrl`, redirects never followed. The Telegram bot
   239	token goes in the request URL *path*, so `TelegramClient.validateBotToken` is a security control,

   245	### Transactional replace (CrowdStrike vuln import)
   246	Per server: `findOrCreateAsset` → `vulnerabilityRepository.deleteByAssetId()` → `saveAll`, all in one `@Transactional`. Idempotent; missing CVEs in the next import = remediation.

See `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md`.

   250	## Test Infrastructure
   251	
   252	JUnit 6, Mockk, AssertJ, `@MicronautTest`. Integration tests run against an **external MariaDB** (no Docker/Testcontainers). **`junit-jupiter-params` is not on the classpath** — `@ParameterizedTest` will not compile; loop inside a plain `@Test`.    277	
   278	`secman_ai_github`, `secman_web_check`, and `secman_intra_mon` are independent Python repositories with their own remotes, **gitignored here** — root `git status` never shows them. 1	# Claude Code Agent Context
     2	
     3	Security requirement, vulnerability and risk management platform.
     4	
     5	## Stack
     6	
     7	- Backend: Kotlin 2.4.20 / Java 25, Micronaut 5.2, Hibernate JPA → `src/backendng/`
     8	- Frontend: Astro 7.3 + React 19 islands, Axios, JWT in the HttpOnly `secman_auth` cookie → `src/frontend/`
     9	- CLI: Kotlin + Picocli 4.7.7, AWS SDK v2 → `src/cli/`
    10	- Mobile relay: Go 1.24, **zero third-party dependencies** (stdlib only, incl. its own RFC 8555 ACME client) → `src/relay/`
    11	- DB: MariaDB 11.4, Flyway + Hibernate auto-migration
    12	- Build: Gradle 9.8.0 (Kotlin DSL)
    13	- MCP: Streamable HTTP / JSON-RPC 2.0. `X-MCP-User-Email` header is **mandatory** on `tools/list` and `tools/call` (only `initialize` and `ping` exempt).
    14	
    15	## Roles (RBAC)
   235	a new event or channel needs no migration and per-channel saves never disturb each other.
   236	Dispatch must stay non-`@Transactional` — it does per-recipient HTTP with a multi-second timeout.
   237	**Security**: the per-user Slack webhook URL is the only user-supplied URL the backend fetches —
   238	host-allowlisted in `SlackClient.validateWebhookUrl`, redirects never followed. The Telegram bot
   239	token goes in the request URL *path*, so `TelegramClient.validateBotToken` is a security control,
   240	not input hygiene. All credentials use `EncryptedStringConverter`, are never returned (only
   241	`…Configured` booleans), and accept `***HIDDEN***` back to mean "keep". Telegram sends with no
   242	`parse_mode` on purpose. CrowdStrike completion is detected by a quiet-period debounce in
   243	`ImportCompletionNotifier` (no last batch exists), AWS account imports publish inline post-commit.
   244	
   245	### Transactional replace (CrowdStrike vuln import)
   246	Per server: `findOrCreateAsset` → `vulnerabilityRepository.deleteByAssetId()` → `saveAll`, all in one `@Transactional`. Idempotent; missing CVEs in the next import = remediation.
   247	
   248	**CRITICAL**: `Asset.vulnerabilities` MUST NOT use `cascade=ALL` or `orphanRemoval=true`. JPA cascade fights the manual delete-insert and silently drops 99% of rows (real incident: 166,812 → 1,819). Use explicit `vulnerabilityRepository.deleteByAssetId()` in the service. See `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md`.
   249	
   250	## Test Infrastructure
   251	
   252	JUnit 6, Mockk, AssertJ, `@MicronautTest`. Integration tests run against an **external MariaDB** (no Docker/Testcontainers). **`junit-jupiter-params` is not on the classpath** — `@ParameterizedTest` will not compile; loop inside a plain `@Test`. Helpers in `src/backendng/src/test/kotlin/com/secman/testutil/`:
   253	- `BaseIntegrationTest` — base for DB-backed tests; datasource comes from `application-test.yml`.
   254	- `TestDataFactory` — admin/vuln/regular user, asset, vulnerability builders.
   255	- `TestAuthHelper` — JWT login → bearer token.
   256	
   257	Run backend tests through `./scripts/runbackendtests.sh` or wrap Gradle with `./scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh --database-only --`. The runner creates and owns a fresh MariaDB schema, sets `TEST_DB_*`, and removes it after the run. Direct Gradle tests without its ownership marker fail before execution.
   258	
   259	```kotlin
   260	class MyIntegrationTest : BaseIntegrationTest() { @Inject lateinit var repo: Repository }
   261	```
   262	
   263	**Frontend unit tier**: `cd src/frontend && npm test` — Node's own runner with native
   264	TypeScript stripping, no test-framework dependency. Tests live beside their module as
   265	`<module>.test.ts`. Imports resolve `.ts` only: Node cannot parse JSX, so pure logic
   266	must be extracted out of `.tsx` into a sibling `.ts` module to be unit-testable (the
   267	resolver hook in `src/frontend/test/` handles extensionless specifiers and raises a
   268	pointed error on `.tsx`). Details in `docs/TESTING.md` §Frontend.
   269	
   270	No persistent `secman_test` setup is needed. Existing application rows are never test input or cleanup targets.
   271	
   272	## File Layout
   273	
   274	`src/backendng/…/com/secman/{domain,controller,service,repository,config,dto,filter,mcp,relay}/` · `src/frontend/src/{pages,components,services,layouts}/` · `src/cli/…/com/secman/cli/{commands,service}/` · `src/shared/…/com/secman/crowdstrike/{client,dto,auth,model}/` (Gradle subproject shared by backendng + cli) · `src/relay/{cmd,internal,deploy}/` (Go). `application.yml` + `email-templates/` under `src/backendng/src/main/resources/`. Env: `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`. Full tree: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §File layout.
   275	
   276	## Extension Clients (`extensions/`)
   277	
   278	`secman_ai_github`, `secman_web_check`, and `secman_intra_mon` are independent Python repositories with their own remotes, **gitignored here** — root `git status` never shows them. Normal builds do not cover them. The first two share the version-1 result contract covered by `/integration-contract-test` and `scripts/check-integration-contract.sh --run`; `secman_intra_mon` uses the legacy REST surface and needs the same manual five-dimension contract check described below. `secman_source` is a separate gitignored local source-review CLI with its own remote; it calls neither SecMan nor the relay, so it has no backend or relay contract to check here.
   279	
   280	`secman_app_ios` (iOS/iPadOS status app, Swift) is a **relay client, not a backend client**: it never calls `/api/…` and holds no secman credential. A change to a secman endpoint cannot break it. What *can* is the relay contract — `com.secman.relay.RelayDtos`, the section names and `SECTION_POLICIES` in `RelaySnapshotBuilder`, or `src/relay/internal/api`. Both envelopes carry a `schemaVersion` for that reason; bump it on a breaking change and update `relaySupportedSnapshotSchemaVersion` in the app. Sweep its surface with `grep -rnE '/api/v1/|/ingest/v1/' extensions/secman_app_ios --include='*.swift'`.
   281	
   282	Always rediscover the surface; a written list means a newly added call gets checked by nobody:
   283	```bash

Version 1 uses `GET /api/integrations/v1/scanners/{id}/subjects` and `POST /api/integrations/v1/runs`; see `docs/INTEGRATION_RESULTS.md`.
   287	
   288	When you change any of those endpoints, verify all five dimensions against the client: **path, HTTP method, request field names, response fields the client reads, and `@Secured` roles / required headers**. Field names matter most — Jackson drops unknown keys without error, so a rename makes the client "succeed" while sending nothing. Update the client's `tests/` too; a test asserting the old shape is drift.
   289	
   290	Fix and commit **inside the extension repo, path-scoped** (`git -C extensions/<repo> commit -m "…" -- <files>`) so pre-existing dirty files are not swallowed. Never `git add -A` / `commit -a`, and **never push** — those repos have their own review. An `@Secured` tightening is a *report*, not a fix: you cannot see which roles the client's service account holds.

   292	## E2E Runner
   293	
   294	**Database safety:** Database-mutating test drivers must be invoked through
   295	`./scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh -- <driver and arguments>`. It creates a
   296	marked disposable schema and restricted database user, copies schema structure

   284	grep -rnE '/api/|"/mcp"|X-MCP-User-Email' extensions --include='*.py' --exclude-dir=.venv
   285	```
   286	As of 2026-09-30: legacy calls remain `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/vulnerabilities/cli-add`, `PUT /api/assets/import`, and `POST /api/scan/upload-nmap`. Version 1 uses `GET /api/integrations/v1/scanners/{id}/subjects` and `POST /api/integrations/v1/runs`; see `docs/INTEGRATION_RESULTS.md`.
   287	
   288	When you change any of those endpoints, verify all five dimensions against the client: **path, HTTP method, request field names, response fields the client reads, and `@Secured` roles / required headers**. Field names matter most — Jackson drops unknown keys without error, so a rename makes the client "succeed" while sending nothing. Update the client's `tests/` too; a test asserting the old shape is drift.
   289	
   290	Fix and commit **inside the extension repo, path-scoped** (`git -C extensions/<repo> commit -m "…" -- <files>`) so pre-existing dirty files are not swallowed. Never `git add -A` / `commit -a`, and **never push** — those repos have their own review. An `@Secured` tightening is a *report*, not a fix: you cannot see which roles the client's service account holds.
   291	
   292	## E2E Runner
   293	
   294	**Database safety:** Database-mutating test drivers must be invoked through
   295	`./scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh -- <driver and arguments>`. It creates a
   296	marked disposable schema and restricted database user, copies schema structure
   297	and Flyway history but no application rows, and starts a separate stack on
   298	18080/14321. It cleans verified abandoned test schemas before a new run and
   299	removes its own schema on exit. Direct driver calls fail closed. Do not delete
   300	an unverified legacy fixture merely because its name matches a test prefix.
   301	The normal 8080/4321 cold-start and stop rules below apply to read-only skills;
   302	the isolated runner owns the lifecycle for mutating skills.
   303	
   304	Triggered by `/e2eexception`, `/admin-asset-e2e`, `/e2ejs`, `/e2evulnexception`, `/e2eeol`, `/account-onboarding`, `/aws-account-workgroup-import`, `/importtest`, `/crowdstrike-vuln-match` skills.
   305	
   306	- **Cold start for read-only skills**: stop the regular backend/frontend via the canonical stop scripts before restarting them. Database-mutating skills never stop or reuse that stack; the isolated runner starts and stops its own services.
   307	- Backend changes (Kotlin/Java) → restart required.
   308	- Frontend changes → Vite hot-reload (no restart).
   309	- Config (`astro.config.mjs`, `application.yml`) → restart.
   310	- Logs: `.e2e-logs/` (gitignored). Max 5 fix iterations.
   311	- **Liveness check is port-bind**, not HTTP: `lsof -iTCP:8080 -sTCP:LISTEN -n -P` (120s budget) and `:4321` (60s budget).
   312	- **Functional checks** use `SECMAN_HOST` for the regular stack or the runner-provided test-only URLs for isolated E2E. Never target regular 8080/4321 for a mutating test.

     9	# SecMan static finalizer
    10	
    11	## When to use
    12	
    13	Use for a static/offline documentation-to-code alignment task in `/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman`, especially when the assignment requires `dev`, mechanically proven documentation edits, a Paperclip trailer, no push, and explicit unavailable-gate reporting.
    14	
    15	Do not use for product behavior changes, service startup, full builds, E2E, credential-backed checks, or resolving an ambiguous backend/client contract without an owner decision.
    16	
    17	## Inputs / context to gather
    18	
    19	1. Read the assigned Paperclip issue, required trailer, intended status/blocker owner, and side-effect limits.
    20	2. Confirm the root branch is `dev`; inspect root plus every relevant independent extension checkout with `git status --short` before edits.
    21	3. Read the claimed documentation sections and the authoritative source/call sites. For Web Check v1, compare `extensions/secman_web_check/src/secman.py` with backend `IntegrationDtos.kt`.
    22	
    23	## Procedure
    24	
    25	1. Treat pre-existing root or extension dirt, merge conflicts, untracked files, and dependency-file changes as user-owned. Do not reset, stash, repair, stage, or include them.
    26	2. Make only documentation changes directly supported by the current source. Never change application behavior merely to make documentation true.
    27	3. Run static in-scope checks: `./scripts/owasp-check.sh`, `./scripts/check-skill-sync.sh` (or `--verbose` when assigned), and `git diff --check`. Run focused suites only when their checkout is clean and the task permits it.
    28	4. If documentation drift is proven, stage only the named paths and commit on `dev` with `Co-Authored-By: Paperclip <noreply@paperclip.ing>`. Do not push.
    29	5. For the `bodyLength` mismatch—Web Check emits `inventory.exposure.bodyLength` while backend `WebExposureInput` does not accept/persist it—stop. The product/integration owner must choose add-to-v1 or remove-from-client; only then align implementation, canonical fixture, and tests in clean checkouts.
    30	6. Make at most one intended Paperclip disposition. Capture the result and GET/read back issue/comment/blocker state. If `blocked` rejects an absent or board-owned `unblockDescriptor`, do not retry the same mutation; use an eligible owner, a real human decision interaction, or a first-class blocker.
    31	7. Report available static results separately from unavailable aggregate/runtime/build/E2E gates.
    32	
    33	## Efficiency plan
    34	
    35	- Preflight branch and all worktree status before source browsing or test execution; this prevents touching user-owned extensions.
    36	- Start from the claimed doc line and its authoritative source instead of broad rewrites.
    37	- Stop aggregate validation immediately when `extensions/secman_visual_check/tests/fixtures/integration-run-v1.json` is absent; retain separately passing focused checks without calling the aggregate gate successful.
    38	
    39	## Pitfalls and fixes
    40	
    41	- `check-integration-contract.sh --run` exits before tests because `integration-run-v1.json` is absent -> report aggregate validation unavailable, not failed product behavior.
    42	- Web Check pytest cannot collect because of existing merge conflicts, such as `src/models.py:178` -> preserve the checkout and report its suite unchecked.
    43	- `bodyLength` exists on one side of the contract only -> do not silently add persistence or drop the client field; require an owner decision.
    44	- Paperclip `blocked` mutation rejected -> preserve successful evidence/comment writes, stop mutation loops, and report the verified remaining state.
    45	
    46	## Verification checklist
    47	
    48	- `dev` was verified before editing and committing.
    49	- Dirty root/extension state is unchanged; commit, if any, is path-scoped and unpushed.
    50	- Documentation claims match inspected authoritative source.
    51	- OWASP, skill-sync, and diff-check results are recorded precisely.
    52	- Missing/unchecked gates are explicitly separated from passes.
    53	- Contract conflicts include the owner decision needed to resume.
    54	- Paperclip outcome has returned-result plus read-back evidence.

The product/integration owner must choose add-to-v1 or remove-from-client; only then align implementation, canonical fixture, and tests in clean checkouts.

If `blocked` rejects an absent or board-owned `unblockDescriptor`, do not retry the same mutation; use an eligible owner, a real human decision interaction, or a first-class blocker.
